chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all of them, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about the divorce of a boy who has not yet reached puberty (had not experienced seminal emission) and his mahr (dowry). He said: If he divorces [her] in accordance with the Sunnah and places the mahr in its proper place, then there is no objection, and it is valid.

key_terms.يَحۡتَلِم: To experience seminal emission (sign of puberty)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the divorce of a minor boy who has not yet reached puberty?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies that a pre-pubescent boy (al-ghulam) possesses the capacity for valid divorce (talaq) and mahr allocation, provided he acts in accordance with the Sunnah. It highlights the Shia juristic view that minority does not invalidate the legal act of divorce, distinguishing it from other contracts that may require a guardian's oversight, thereby affirming the boy's independent legal agency in marital dissolution.
